newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power quiet amid holiday closures.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power quiet amid holiday closures.

text.p: The spot market for power in the western U.S. saw little activity, with utilities closed for the Martin Luther King holiday, trade sources said Monday.
"Everything was already pre-scheduled through Tuesday," explained one trader.

Market sources said spot prices were unlikely to rebound this week from the sharp drop seen Friday given forecasts for normal to slightly above-normal temperatures in both the Northwest and Southwest.
Recent rain in the Pacific Northwest was also seen adding to already ample supplies of hydroelectric generation.
"As early as February last year we saw prices at $7.00-8.00 (per megawatt hour) on-peak and $4.00-5.00 off-peak," said one trader.
"This may be happening again," he added.
Next-day firm, peak electricity at the California-Oregon border (COB) was notionally quoted $15.00-18.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), while off-peak was at $9.00-10.00.
Firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) fell to $14.00-15.00, while off-peak was at $10.00-11.00.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity was quoted $16.00-19.00, while off-peak was at $10.00-11.00 per MWh.
Next-day firm, peak prices at Four Corners were quoted at $15.00-18.00, while off-peak was at $9.00-11.00.
